items.followUp: Define density and write its SI unit.

rubric.why: Pressure is defined as force acting per unit area.
rubric.description: Defines pressure as force per unit area.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that pressure is force divided by area.

rubric.why: The SI unit of pressure is the pascal, equivalent to one newton per square metre.
rubric.description: Gives the SI unit of pressure.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for pascal (Pa) or its equivalent unit.

modelAnswer: Pressure is the force acting normally per unit area of a surface.
Its SI unit is the pascal (Pa), equal to N m⁻².

items.followUp: A force of 120 N acts normally on an area of 0.03 m². Calculate the pressure.

rubric.why: The mass must be in kilograms and the temperature rise is 70 °C; the heater power is 1000 W.
rubric.description: Identifies the relevant data in SI units.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for correctly using the mass, temperature change, water's specific heat capacity and heater power.

rubric.why: Heat supplied to the water is calculated using its mass, specific heat capacity and temperature rise.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct formula for heat energy.
Award 1 mark for the correct heat value with unit.

rubric.why: Power is the heat energy supplied per unit time, so time is energy divided by power.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for correctly rearranging the power relation to find time.

rubric.description: Gives the required time with unit.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct final answer.

modelAnswer: Given: P = 1000 W, m = 200 g = 0.2 kg, initial temperature = 20 °C, final temperature = 90 °C.
Temperature rise, ΔT = 90 − 20 = 70 °C; specific heat capacity of water, c = 4200 J kg⁻¹ °C⁻¹.
Heat required: Q = mcΔT.
Power: P = Q/t, so t = Q/P.

items.followUp: A screw gauge has 100 divisions on its circular scale and a pitch of 1 mm. Find its least count.

rubric.why: Least count is the pitch divided by the number of divisions on the circular scale.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct formula.

rubric.description: Calculates the least count with unit.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct result and unit.

modelAnswer: Least count = pitch / number of divisions on circular scale.
Least count = 0.5 mm / 50 = 0.01 mm.

items.followUp: State two rules for identifying significant figures in a measured quantity.

rubric.description: Gives a valid rule about non-zero digits.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that all non-zero digits are significant.

accept: zeros between nonzero digits are significant
zeros to the left are not significant
trailing zeros after decimal are significant
rubric.why: The other stated rule must correctly describe a class of zeros and its significance.
rubric.description: Gives another valid rule about zeros.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correct rule, such as captive zeros being significant, leading zeros not being significant, or trailing zeros after a decimal point being significant.

modelAnswer: All non-zero digits in a number are significant.
Zeros between non-zero digits are significant; leading zeros are not significant.

rubric.why: Velocity is displacement per unit time and has unit m s⁻¹.
rubric.description: States the definition or formula for velocity.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for correctly identifying velocity as rate of change of displacement.

rubric.why: Acceleration is change in velocity per unit time and has unit m s⁻².
rubric.description: States the definition or formula for acceleration.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for correctly identifying acceleration as rate of change of velocity.

modelAnswer: Velocity is the rate of change of displacement with time; its SI unit is m s⁻¹.
Acceleration is the rate of change of velocity with time; its SI unit is m s⁻².

items.followUp: Define inertia and state the quantity on which it depends.

rubric.why: Momentum is the product of an object's mass and velocity.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating the product of mass and velocity.

rubric.why: Force is a push or pull that changes or tends to change an object's state of rest or motion; it can also be defined as the rate of change of momentum.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correct definition of force.

modelAnswer: Momentum is the product of the mass of a body and its velocity: p = mv.
Force is a push or pull that changes or tends to change the state of rest or motion of a body.

items.followUp: Convert 5 km h⁻¹ to m s⁻¹.

rubric.why: Conversion requires replacing one kilometre by 1000 metres and one hour by 3600 seconds.
rubric.description: Shows the conversion of kilometre and hour into SI units.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct conversion setup.

rubric.why: Dividing 1000 by 3600 gives 5/18 m s⁻¹, approximately 0.2778 m s⁻¹.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct answer with unit.

items.followUp: Define pressure and state its SI unit.

rubric.why: Pressure is the normal force acting on each unit of area.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that pressure is force per unit area.

rubric.why: Pressure is calculated by dividing force by area.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct formula.

modelAnswer: Pressure is the force acting normally per unit area of a surface.
Pressure = force / area, or P = F/A.
